reuse.why: Most server sites use the new getWorstCaseAmount and the tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but the API model writes its own private getExpectedAmount instead of calling the shared helper.

duplication.why: api-models.ts re-implements the null/number/range dispatch with the old furthest-from-zero rule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own null/number/range dispatch.

placement.why: The rule is placed in shared/schedules, but a second copy of it lives privately in server/api-models.ts.

scope.why: Changes stay on the amount rule and the API field; the Balance.tsx op threading and three release notes (one describing a superseded rule) are slightly loose.

maintainability.why: The API's expectedAmount already contradicts the final lowest-value rule because it has its own copy, preview transactions ignore the approximate rule, and only one desktop caller passes op to getScheduledAmount.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts getExpectedAmount bypasses getWorstCaseAmount; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in shared/schedules.ts calls only getRangeAmount inside its own dispatch; SchedulesTable, mobile schedule views and useScheduleEdit call getScheduledAmount without op.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts getExpectedAmount is the shared amount dispatch renamed and rewritten inline (Math.abs comparison instead of getRangeAmount), so it drifted from the shared rule.

abstraction_drift.where: op parameter added to getWorstCaseAmount and getScheduledAmount with an isapprox branch; bypassing sites: api-models getExpectedAmount (re-implementation), computeSchedulePreviewTransactions (own dispatch, no op), and desktop getScheduledAmount callers other than Balance.tsx that omit op.
